answers.question: How many days of earned leave do confirmed employees get per year?
answers.ground_truth: Confirmed employees get 18 days of Earned Leave per calendar year.
answers.answer: Confirmed employees are entitled to 18 days of Earned Leave per calendar year.
contexts:
Leave Policy > 4. Types of Leave and Entitlements > 4.1. Earned Leave (EL) / Annual Leave

All confirmed employees are entitled to 18 days of Earned Leave per calendar year. EL is credited in advance on 1st January every year. Employees who join mid-year receive pro-rated EL at the rate of 1.5 days per completed month of service remaining in the year. EL can be availed in a minimum block of 1 day. A maximum of 3 consecutive weeks (15 working days) can be taken at one time. Employees must apply for EL at least 7 working days in advance through the HRMS portal. Approval is subject to manager discretion based on project requirements. Unused EL up to a maximum of 10 days can be carried forward to the next calendar year. Any balance exceeding 10 days at year-end will lapse. Encashment of EL is permitted only at the time of resignation, retirement, or termination at the rate of basic salary divided by 26 multiplied by the number of days encashed.

Employee FAQ > 1. Leave and Holidays

How many leaves do I get in a year? Confirmed employees get 18 days of Earned Leave, 12 days of Sick Leave, and 6 days of Casual Leave per calendar year, plus 12 public holidays. See the Leave Policy for details.

Can I carry forward unused leave? Only Earned Leave carries forward, up to a maximum of 10 days; anything above that lapses at year end. Sick Leave and Casual Leave lapse every December.

How do I apply for leave? Through the HRMS portal at hrms.rutujatalentnexus.in. Planned leave needs 7 working days' advance application; for emergencies, notify your manager before 9:30 AM and file the request the same day.

What is the maternity and paternity leave entitlement? Maternity leave is 26 weeks of paid leave for the first two children (12 weeks for the third onward). Paternity leave is 15 days, to be taken within 3 months of birth or adoption.

Which festival holidays do we get? The 12 public holidays include national holidays plus Maharashtra festival holidays such as Gudi Padwa, Maharashtra Day (1 May), Ganesh Chaturthi, and Diwali. The exact list is published on the intranet each January.

Leave Policy > At a Glance

Per calendar year: 18 days Earned Leave, 12 Sick Leave, 6 Casual Leave, and 12 public holidays (including Gudi Padwa, Maharashtra Day, and Ganesh Chaturthi). Maternity leave is 26 weeks, paternity 15 days, bereavement 5 days, plus 1 menstrual leave day per month. Up to 10 EL days carry forward; apply via hrms.rutujatalentnexus.in.

Leave Policy > 4. Types of Leave and Entitlements > 4.3. Casual Leave (CL)

All employees are entitled to 6 days of Casual Leave per calendar year for urgent personal matters, emergencies, or unforeseen circumstances. CL is credited on 1st January. CL cannot be combined with EL or taken for more than 2 consecutive days. CL must be applied in advance where possible or on the same day of absence through the HRMS portal with manager notification. Unused CL at year-end will lapse and cannot be encashed or carried forward.

Probation and Confirmation Policy > 6. Probation Review and Confirmation > 6.1. Confirmation

If the employee has met or exceeded the expected standards across all evaluation criteria, the manager recommends confirmation. HR issues a formal Confirmation Letter to the employee within 5 working days of the probation end date. The confirmation is effective from the date immediately following the end of the probation period. Upon confirmation, the employee becomes eligible for all benefits and entitlements applicable to confirmed employees as described elsewhere in the HR policies.

answers.question: When do I need a medical certificate for sick leave?
answers.ground_truth: A medical certificate is needed for absences of 3 or more consecutive days, submitted to HR within 2 working days of resuming duty.
answers.answer: For absences of 3 or more consecutive days of sick leave, a medical certificate from a registered medical practitioner must be submitted to HR within 2 working days of resuming duty. Additionally, Sick Leave taken during the notice period must be supported by a medical certificate.
contexts:
Leave Policy > 4. Types of Leave and Entitlements > 4.2. Sick Leave (SL)

All employees including those on probation are entitled to 12 days of Sick Leave per calendar year. SL is credited on 1st January each year. Pro-rated SL is provided to employees joining mid-year at 1 day per completed month. Sick leave can be availed for personal illness, injury, or medical procedures. For absences of 1 to 2 days, self-declaration via the HRMS portal is sufficient. For absences of 3 or more consecutive days, a medical certificate from a registered medical practitioner must be submitted to HR within 2 working days of resuming duty. Sick Leave cannot be carried forward or encashed. Misuse of sick leave will be treated as misconduct and may result in disciplinary action.

Leave Policy > 7. Leave During Notice Period

Employees who have submitted their resignation are discouraged from availing EL or CL during the notice period except under compelling personal circumstances with prior HR approval. SL during the notice period must be supported by a medical certificate. If leave is availed during the notice period, the notice period will be extended by the equivalent number of leave days taken unless agreed otherwise in writing by HR.

Leave Policy > 4. Types of Leave and Entitlements > 4.7. Menstrual Leave

Rutuja Talent Nexus Pvt. Ltd. provides 1 day of paid Menstrual Leave per month to all cisgender female employees and transgender employees who menstruate. This leave is in addition to other leave entitlements. No medical certificate or proof is required. The employee must notify their manager by 9:30 AM on the day of availing this leave. Menstrual Leave cannot be accumulated or encashed.

Leave Policy > 4. Types of Leave and Entitlements > 4.6. Bereavement Leave

Employees are entitled to 5 days of paid Bereavement Leave in the event of the death of an immediate family member. Immediate family includes spouse or partner, children, parents, parents-in-law, and siblings. For the death of a grandparent or close relative not covered above, 2 days of paid Bereavement Leave is granted at the discretion of HR. Employees must notify their manager and HR immediately and submit supporting documentation such as a death certificate upon return to work. Bereavement Leave cannot be carried forward or encashed.

Work From Home Policy > 5. Extended Remote Work

In addition to the standard 2 WFH days per week, employees may apply for Extended Remote Work of up to 30 working days per calendar year. Extended remote work may be required for reasons such as relocation within India, medical necessity with doctor's certificate, or care of a dependent family member. The application must be submitted through HRMS with justification and supporting documents at least 10 working days in advance. Approval requires sign-off from the reporting manager and HR Business Partner. Extended remote work beyond 30 days in a year requires additional approval from the department head and HR Director.

answers.question: How long is maternity leave for my first child?
answers.ground_truth: Maternity leave is 26 weeks of paid leave for the first two children, for employees who worked at least 80 days in the preceding 12 months.
answers.answer: Female employees who have worked for at least 80 days in the 12 months preceding their expected delivery date are entitled to 26 weeks of paid Maternity Leave for the first two children.
contexts:
Leave Policy > 4. Types of Leave and Entitlements > 4.4. Maternity Leave

In accordance with the Maternity Benefit (Amendment) Act 2017, all female employees who have worked for at least 80 days in the 12 months preceding their expected delivery date are entitled to 26 weeks of paid Maternity Leave for the first two children. For the third child onwards, the entitlement is 12 weeks. In case of miscarriage or medical termination of pregnancy, 6 weeks of paid leave is granted from the date of the miscarriage. In case of a tubectomy operation, 2 weeks of paid leave is granted. For adoption of a child below 3 months of age, a commissioning mother is entitled to 12 weeks of Maternity Leave. The employee must submit a written intimation to HR at least 8 weeks before the expected date of delivery along with a medical certificate confirming the expected due date. During maternity leave, the employee is entitled to full pay equivalent to the average daily wage for the preceding 3 months. Maternity Leave cannot be clubbed with any other leave type except EL under specific medical circumstances with HR approval.

Leave Policy > 4. Types of Leave and Entitlements > 4.5. Paternity Leave

All male employees and same-sex partners are entitled to 15 days of paid Paternity Leave to be availed within 3 months of the birth or adoption of a child. This is applicable for up to 2 children. The employee must notify HR and the reporting manager at least 4 weeks before the expected date of availing the leave. Paternity Leave can be taken in one continuous stretch or split into two tranches within the 3-month window. It cannot be carried forward or encashed.

Leave Policy > At a Glance

Group Health Insurance and Mediclaim Policy > 11. Continuity of Coverage During Leave

Employees on approved leave including maternity leave, paternity leave, or medical leave continue to be covered under the group mediclaim policy for the duration of their approved leave.

answers.question: What is the notice period for a confirmed employee?
answers.ground_truth: Confirmed employees must serve a notice period of 3 months from the date of formal resignation.
answers.answer: Confirmed employees are required to serve a notice period of 3 months (or 90 days) from the date of formal resignation. Notice period buyout is also possible with management and HR approval.
contexts:
Resignation and Exit Policy > 4. Notice Period

Employees on probation are required to serve a notice period of 2 weeks, as defined in the Probation and Confirmation Policy. Confirmed employees are required to serve a notice period of 3 months from the date of formal resignation. The notice period begins from the date of resignation submission and acknowledgment by HR. Employees must remain fully productive, committed, and professional throughout the notice period.

Probation and Confirmation Policy > 9. Notice Period During Probation

During the probation period, the notice period for voluntary resignation by the employee is 2 weeks. The notice period for company-initiated separation during probation is also 2 weeks, except in cases of gross misconduct where summary dismissal without notice applies. This is distinct from the confirmed employee notice period, which is 90 days (3 months) as stated in the offer letter and Resignation and Exit Policy.

Probation and Confirmation Policy > At a Glance

Standard probation is 6 months (3 months for Bands 1-3), extendable once by up to 3 months. The confirmation letter is issued within 5 working days of the probation end date, and the notice period during probation is 2 weeks for either side. Confirmation is contingent on a clean background verification.

Resignation and Exit Policy > At a Glance

Notice period is 2 weeks on probation and 3 months once confirmed; buyout is possible with approval. Knowledge transfer and exit clearance are mandatory, Full and Final settlement completes within 45 days, and relieving and experience letters follow within 7 working days of FnF. Rehire is possible after a 1-year gap for employees in good standing.

Employee FAQ > 6. Joining, Probation, and Exit

How long is probation? 6 months as standard, or 3 months for Bands 1-3, extendable once by up to 3 months. Confirmation requires a clean background verification.

What is my notice period? 2 weeks while on probation and 3 months once confirmed. Notice period buyout is possible with management and HR approval.

When do I get my final settlement and relieving letter? Full and Final settlement is processed within 45 days of your last working day, and the relieving and experience letters are issued within 7 working days after FnF.

Can I refer a friend for a job? Yes. Submit the referral through the HRMS Referral Module before the candidate applies. The referral bonus is paid 50 percent when the hire completes 3 months and 50 percent at 6 months.

answers.question: How long does full and final settlement take after I leave?
answers.ground_truth: Full and Final settlement completes within 45 days of exit.
answers.answer: The full and final settlement is processed within 45 days of the last working day, subject to the completion of the exit clearance process.
contexts:

The full and final settlement will be processed within 45 days of the last working day, subject to completion of the exit clearance process. The FnF amount will be credited directly to the employee's registered bank account. The settlement slip will be shared via the employee's personal email provided during exit.

The Full and Final Settlement payout for separating employees is processed within 45 days of the last working day, subject to completion of the exit clearance process. The FnF payslip is issued through HRMS and reflects all dues and deductions including outstanding salary, earned leave encashment, notice period recovery or payment, outstanding advances, and any other adjustments. Gratuity, if applicable, is paid separately in accordance with the Payment of Gratuity Act 1972, within 30 days of the last working day.

Knowledge transfer and exit clearance are mandatory, Full and Final settlement completes within 45 days, and relieving and experience letters follow within 7 working days of FnF. When do I get my final settlement and relieving letter? Full and Final settlement is processed within 45 days of your last working day, and the relieving and experience letters are issued within 7 working days after FnF.

Upon successful completion of the exit clearance process and full and final settlement, the employee will receive a Relieving Letter confirming the last working day and a Certificate of Experience confirming the period of employment and designation held. answers.question: How many days can I work from home per week?
answers.ground_truth: Up to 2 days per week under the hybrid model, available after confirmation with a performance rating of 3 or above.
answers.answer:
Rutuja Talent Nexus follows a hybrid model allowing up to 2 WFH days per week, with a minimum of 3 days in the office. 

Eligibility conditions:
- Available after confirmation.
- Requires a performance rating of 3 or above.

Exceptions and rules:
- Designated standard WFH days are Tuesday and Thursday, while office days are Monday, Wednesday, and Friday.
- Team leads and managers may adjust office or WFH days based on project requirements, client meetings, or sprint cycles with a minimum notice of 48 hours. 
- Business requirements take precedence, and WFH days are not fixed and non-negotiable.
contexts:
Work From Home Policy > At a Glance

Hybrid model: minimum 3 office days per week with up to 2 WFH days, available after confirmation with a performance rating of 3 or above. Extended remote work of up to 30 working days per year can be requested. Company laptop and VPN are mandatory, with core hours of 10:00 AM to 4:00 PM. A one-time home-office setup allowance is provided.

Employee FAQ > 3. Work From Home and Attendance

How many days can I work from home? Rutuja Talent Nexus follows a hybrid model: minimum 3 days in office per week, up to 2 WFH days. You must be confirmed with a performance rating of 3 or above to be eligible.

What are the working hours? 9:00 AM to 6:00 PM with a 15-minute grace period, and core hours of 10:00 AM to 4:00 PM on WFH days. Flexi-time windows are available with manager approval.

Can I work remotely for a longer stretch? Yes, Extended Remote Work of up to 30 working days per calendar year can be requested for relocation, medical, or family-care reasons. See the Work From Home Policy.

Work From Home Policy > 3. Standard Hybrid Work Model

Rutuja Talent Nexus follows a Hybrid Work Model. All eligible employees are required to be present in the office for a minimum of 3 days per week. The designated office days are Monday, Wednesday, and Friday. The standard work-from-home days are Tuesday and Thursday. Team leads and managers may adjust office or WFH days based on project requirements, client meetings, or sprint cycles with a minimum notice of 48 hours. Employees must not assume that WFH days are fixed and non-negotiable. Business requirements take precedence.

Work From Home Policy > 5. Extended Remote Work

In addition to the standard 2 WFH days per week, employees may apply for Extended Remote Work of up to 30 working days per calendar year. Extended remote work may be required for reasons such as relocation within India, medical necessity with doctor's certificate, or care of a dependent family member. The application must be submitted through HRMS with justification and supporting documents at least 10 working days in advance. Approval requires sign-off from the reporting manager and HR Business Partner. Extended remote work beyond 30 days in a year requires additional approval from the department head and HR Director.

Work From Home Policy > 11. Revocation of WFH Privilege

The WFH arrangement is a privilege and not an employee right. It may be revoked entirely or partially in the following circumstances: sustained underperformance during remote work, security incidents caused by negligence during WFH, violation of any clause of this policy, business requirements mandating full in-office presence, or employee being placed on a Performance Improvement Plan. Revocation will be communicated in writing with a minimum of 5 working days notice.

answers.question: Can I work from home while I am on probation?
answers.ground_truth: Employees on probation are not eligible for regular WFH unless specifically approved by HR due to exceptional circumstances.
answers.answer: Employees on probation are not eligible for regular WFH arrangements unless specifically approved by HR due to exceptional circumstances.
contexts:
Work From Home Policy > 4. Eligibility Criteria

To be eligible for the standard WFH arrangement, an employee must have completed their probation period (3 or 6 months, as applicable per the Probation and Confirmation Policy) and received confirmation of employment. The employee must have a performance rating of 3 or above in the most recent appraisal cycle. The employee must have a suitable home workspace with a reliable internet connection of at least 25 Mbps, a dedicated work area free from distractions, and access to required tools and systems. Employees with active Performance Improvement Plans are not eligible for WFH until the PIP is successfully closed.

Probation and Confirmation Policy > At a Glance

Standard probation is 6 months (3 months for Bands 1-3), extendable once by up to 3 months. The confirmation letter is issued within 5 working days of the probation end date, and the notice period during probation is 2 weeks for either side. Confirmation is contingent on a clean background verification.

Work From Home Policy > At a Glance

Hybrid model: minimum 3 office days per week with up to 2 WFH days, available after confirmation with a performance rating of 3 or above. Extended remote work of up to 30 working days per year can be requested. Company laptop and VPN are mandatory, with core hours of 10:00 AM to 4:00 PM. A one-time home-office setup allowance is provided.

Work From Home Policy > 2. Scope

This policy applies to all confirmed full-time employees of Rutuja Talent Nexus Pvt. Ltd. Employees on probation are not eligible for regular WFH arrangements unless specifically approved by HR due to exceptional circumstances. Contract staff and third-party vendors working on Rutuja Talent Nexus premises are not covered under this policy.

Internal Transfer Policy > 7. Probationary Period in New Role

All employees who transfer to a new role under the IJP process are subject to a 60-day probationary period in the new role. During this period, the employee and new manager review whether the transition is working effectively. If the employee does not meet the expectations of the new role within 60 days, HR will discuss options including returning to a suitable role or exploring other alternatives. The employee is not eligible to apply for further internal transfers during the 60-day probationary period in the new role.

answers.question: When is my salary credited?
answers.ground_truth: Salary is credited by the last working day of the month.
answers.answer: Salary for each calendar month is credited to the employee's registered bank account on or before the last working day of that month. In months where the last working day falls on a public holiday or weekend, the salary is credited on the preceding working day. For new joiners whose joining date falls after the payroll cut-off date, the salary for the partial month of joining is processed along with the following month's payroll.
contexts:
Payroll and Salary Processing Policy > 3. Salary Credit Date

Salary for each calendar month is credited to the employee's registered bank account on or before the last working day of that month. In months where the last working day falls on a public holiday or weekend, salary is credited on the preceding working day. For new joiners whose joining date falls after the payroll cut-off date defined in Section 4, the salary for the partial month of joining is processed along with the following month's payroll. New joiners are informed of this at the time of onboarding.

Compensation and Benefits Policy > 5. Salary Disbursement

Salaries are credited to the employee's designated bank account on the last working day of each month. Salary slips are generated and made available on the HRMS portal by the 5th of the following month. Employees must ensure their bank account details and PAN card information in HRMS are accurate and up to date. In case of salary discrepancies, employees must raise a query with the Finance team through the HRMS helpdesk within 5 working days of salary credit.

Employee FAQ > 2. Salary and Payroll

When is salary credited? On or before the last working day of each month, to the bank account registered in HRMS.

When are payslips available? On the HRMS Payroll section by the 5th of the following month. The payslip password is your date of birth in DDMMYYYY format.

What is deducted from my salary? Employee Provident Fund (12 percent of basic salary), Professional Tax (Rs. 200 per month, Rs. 300 in February, per the Maharashtra slab), and TDS based on your chosen tax regime and declarations.

I found an error in my salary. What do I do? Raise a Payroll Query in HRMS within 30 days of the payslip. The payroll team responds within 5 working days, and confirmed corrections are paid with the next cycle.

Can I take a salary advance? Confirmed employees with 12 or more months of service can request an interest-free advance (up to 1 month's gross salary for Bands 1-3). An emergency advance of up to Rs. 25,000 is available regardless of band. See the Salary Advance Policy.

Payroll and Salary Processing Policy > 17. Payroll Calendar

The payroll team publishes an annual Payroll Calendar at the start of each financial year in April, listing the cut-off dates, salary credit dates, and reimbursement submission deadlines for all 12 months. The Payroll Calendar is available on the HRMS Payroll section and is also shared on the company intranet.

Payroll and Salary Processing Policy > At a Glance

Salary is credited by the last working day of the month; the payroll cut-off is the 20th. Payslips are on HRMS by the 5th, tax declarations are submitted each April, and payroll queries must be raised within 30 days of the payslip. Full and Final settlement completes within 45 days of exit. Maharashtra Professional Tax applies (Rs. 200 per month; Rs. 300 in February).

answers.question: What are the standard office hours and the grace period?
answers.ground_truth: Standard hours are 9:00 AM to 6:00 PM with a 15-minute grace period.
answers.answer: Standard office hours are 9:00 AM to 6:00 PM, Monday through Friday, with a 15-minute grace period (arrivals up to 9:15 AM will not be flagged).
contexts:
Attendance Policy > At a Glance

Standard hours are 9:00 AM to 6:00 PM with a 15-minute grace period; clock in via biometric or the HRMS app. Flexi-time windows (8-5, 9-6, 10-7) need manager approval. Attendance reconciles with payroll on the 20th of each month; proxy attendance is serious misconduct.

Attendance Policy > 3. Standard Working Hours

The standard working hours at Rutuja Talent Nexus Pvt. Ltd. are 9:00 AM to 6:00 PM, Monday through Friday, inclusive of a 1-hour unpaid lunch break. The net productive working hours expected per day are 8 hours. The standard working week consists of 5 days totalling 40 hours of productive work. Employees are expected to be at their workstations and ready to begin work by 9:00 AM. The core hours during which all employees must be available for meetings, collaboration, and client calls are 10:00 AM to 4:00 PM. Outside of core hours, employees with manager approval may exercise flexi-start options as described in Section 6.

Attendance Policy > 5. Late Coming Policy

Employees are expected to arrive at the workplace by 9:00 AM. A grace period of 15 minutes is allowed, meaning arrivals up to 9:15 AM will not be flagged. Arrivals between 9:16 AM and 10:00 AM will be recorded as late. Arrivals after 10:00 AM without prior intimation will be treated as a half-day absence. Three late arrivals in a calendar month will be treated as one half-day Loss of Pay deduction. Chronic late coming defined as more than 5 instances in a month will trigger a formal counselling session with the reporting manager and HR. Repeated patterns of late coming post-counselling may result in written warning or disciplinary action. Employees who anticipate being late due to unavoidable circumstances such as medical emergencies or public transport disruptions must notify their reporting manager via message or call before 9:15 AM.

Attendance Policy > 6. Flexi-Time Arrangement

Employees may opt for a flexi-start time with prior written approval from their reporting manager. Approved flexi-time windows are 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM, 9:00 AM to 6:00 PM (standard), or 10:00 AM to 7:00 PM. The core hours of 10:00 AM to 4:00 PM remain mandatory regardless of the chosen flexi window. Flexi-time arrangements are reviewed quarterly and can be revoked by the manager if project demands require it. Flexi-time does not apply during client visits, team events, or mandatory all-hands meetings.

Employee FAQ > 3. Work From Home and Attendance

How many days can I work from home? Rutuja Talent Nexus follows a hybrid model: minimum 3 days in office per week, up to 2 WFH days. You must be confirmed with a performance rating of 3 or above to be eligible.

What are the working hours? 9:00 AM to 6:00 PM with a 15-minute grace period, and core hours of 10:00 AM to 4:00 PM on WFH days. Flexi-time windows are available with manager approval.

Can I work remotely for a longer stretch? Yes, Extended Remote Work of up to 30 working days per calendar year can be requested for relocation, medical, or family-care reasons. See the Work From Home Policy.

answers.question: How long is the probation period?
answers.ground_truth: Standard probation is 6 months, or 3 months for Bands 1-3, and can be extended once by up to 3 months.
answers.answer: The standard probation period is 6 months from the date of joining. For roles at Band 1 to Band 3, the probation period is 3 months from the date of joining. For roles at Band 4 to Band 6 and Band 7 and above, it is 6 months. The probation period may be extended once by up to 3 months. Additionally, employees who transfer to a new role under the IJP process are subject to a 60-day probationary period in the new role.
contexts:
Probation and Confirmation Policy > At a Glance

Standard probation is 6 months (3 months for Bands 1-3), extendable once by up to 3 months. The confirmation letter is issued within 5 working days of the probation end date, and the notice period during probation is 2 weeks for either side. Confirmation is contingent on a clean background verification.

Probation and Confirmation Policy > 3. Probation Period Duration

The standard probation period at Rutuja Talent Nexus is 6 months from the date of joining. For roles at Band 1 to Band 3, the probation period is 3 months from the date of joining. For roles at Band 4 to Band 6, the probation period is 6 months from the date of joining. For roles at Band 7 and above, the probation period is 6 months from the date of joining. The probation period begins on the date of joining as documented in the offer letter and in HRMS, and ends on the last day of the applicable period unless extended as described in Section 6.

Employee FAQ > 6. Joining, Probation, and Exit

How long is probation? 6 months as standard, or 3 months for Bands 1-3, extendable once by up to 3 months. Confirmation requires a clean background verification.

What is my notice period? 2 weeks while on probation and 3 months once confirmed. Notice period buyout is possible with management and HR approval.

When do I get my final settlement and relieving letter? Full and Final settlement is processed within 45 days of your last working day, and the relieving and experience letters are issued within 7 working days after FnF.

Can I refer a friend for a job? Yes. Submit the referral through the HRMS Referral Module before the candidate applies. The referral bonus is paid 50 percent when the hire completes 3 months and 50 percent at 6 months.

Probation and Confirmation Policy > 9. Notice Period During Probation

During the probation period, the notice period for voluntary resignation by the employee is 2 weeks. The notice period for company-initiated separation during probation is also 2 weeks, except in cases of gross misconduct where summary dismissal without notice applies. This is distinct from the confirmed employee notice period, which is 90 days (3 months) as stated in the offer letter and Resignation and Exit Policy.

Internal Transfer Policy > 7. Probationary Period in New Role

All employees who transfer to a new role under the IJP process are subject to a 60-day probationary period in the new role. During this period, the employee and new manager review whether the transition is working effectively. If the employee does not meet the expectations of the new role within 60 days, HR will discuss options including returning to a suitable role or exploring other alternatives. The employee is not eligible to apply for further internal transfers during the 60-day probationary period in the new role.

answers.question: What is the hotel limit per night when travelling to a Tier-1 city?
answers.ground_truth: The hotel limit is Rs. 4,000 per night in Tier-1 cities.
answers.answer:
For Tier-1 cities (including Bangalore, Mumbai, Delhi, Hyderabad, Pune, and Chennai), the maximum hotel allowance is Rs. 4,000 per night inclusive of taxes. 

Additional conditions:
- Hotels must be booked through the company travel portal wherever available.
- The hotel must be within a reasonable distance from the work location.
- Luxury hotels and resorts are not permitted unless no standard accommodation is available in the vicinity and prior approval has been obtained.
contexts:
Travel and Expense Policy > 4. Domestic Travel Entitlements > 4.3. Hotel Accommodation

Hotel accommodation entitlements are based on the city tier of the travel destination. For Tier 1 cities including Bangalore, Mumbai, Delhi, Hyderabad, Pune, and Chennai, the maximum hotel allowance is Rs. 4,000 per night inclusive of taxes. For Tier 2 cities and other locations, the maximum is Rs. 2,500 per night. Hotels must be booked through the company travel portal wherever available. The hotel must be within reasonable distance from the work location. Luxury hotels and resorts are not permitted unless no standard accommodation is available in the vicinity and prior approval has been obtained.

Travel and Expense Policy > 4. Domestic Travel Entitlements > 4.4. Daily Allowance

A daily allowance is provided to cover meals, local transport, and incidental expenses during domestic travel. For Tier 1 cities, the daily allowance is Rs. 800 per day. For Tier 2 cities and other locations, it is Rs. 600 per day. Daily allowance is paid for each full day of travel including the day of departure and return if travel extends beyond 12 hours. No receipts are required for daily allowance claims. Daily allowance is not payable when the company provides accommodation and meals directly.

Travel and Expense Policy > At a Glance

All business travel needs pre-approval; domestic flights are economy only, booked from Nashik (Ozar) Airport, Mumbai, or Pune. Hotel limits are Rs. 4,000 per night in Tier-1 cities and Rs. 2,500 elsewhere; daily allowance is Rs. 800/600. Submit claims within 10 working days of return; advances up to 80 percent of estimated cost.

Travel and Expense Policy > 5. International Travel Entitlements

International travel must be approved by the department head and HR Director as described in Section 3. Air travel for international trips up to 6 hours is in economy class. For flights exceeding 6 hours, premium economy class may be booked with department head approval. Business class for international travel requires CEO approval. Hotel accommodation for international travel is reimbursed up to USD 150 per night or equivalent local currency. A foreign daily allowance of USD 75 per day is provided for meals and incidentals. Employees must use the company's forex card issued by the Finance team for international travel expenses. Personal credit card usage is permitted only when the forex card is not usable and must be supported by exchange rate documentation.

Travel and Expense Policy > 4. Domestic Travel Entitlements > 4.5. Local Transport

For travel to and from airports, railway stations, and client sites, employees may use taxis booked through approved cab aggregators such as Uber or Ola. Auto-rickshaws, metro, and buses may be used for short distances and are fully reimbursable. Personal vehicle use for official travel is reimbursable at Rs. 8 per kilometre for two-wheelers and Rs. 12 per kilometre for four-wheelers with prior approval.

answers.question: How soon must I submit a travel expense claim?
answers.ground_truth: Claims must be submitted within 10 working days of return.
answers.answer: Employees must submit expense claims through the HRMS Expense module within 10 working days of returning from travel. Claims submitted after 30 days of travel will not be reimbursed without written justification approved by HR.
contexts:
Travel and Expense Policy > 6. Expense Reimbursement Process

Employees must submit expense claims through the HRMS Expense module within 10 working days of returning from travel. Claims submitted after 30 days of travel will not be reimbursed without written justification approved by HR. All claims must be accompanied by original receipts, invoices, or boarding passes as applicable. Daily allowance claims do not require receipts. Expense claims are reviewed and approved by the reporting manager within 3 working days. Finance processes approved claims within 15 working days of manager approval. Reimbursements are credited directly to the employee's registered salary bank account.

Travel and Expense Policy > 10. Roles and Responsibilities

The employee is responsible for planning cost-effective travel, obtaining approvals in advance, maintaining receipts, and submitting claims within the stipulated timeline. The reporting manager is responsible for approving travel and expense claims within 3 working days and ensuring travel is genuinely business-related. Finance is responsible for processing approved claims within 15 working days and maintaining expense records. HR is responsible for policy administration, auditing claims, and addressing exceptions.

Travel and Expense Policy > At a Glance

All business travel needs pre-approval; domestic flights are economy only, booked from Nashik (Ozar) Airport, Mumbai, or Pune. Hotel limits are Rs. 4,000 per night in Tier-1 cities and Rs. 2,500 elsewhere; daily allowance is Rs. 800/600. Submit claims within 10 working days of return; advances up to 80 percent of estimated cost.

Travel and Expense Policy > 8. Travel Advances

Employees may request a travel advance of up to 80 percent of the estimated travel cost through the HRMS Travel module at least 5 working days before departure. The advance will be credited to the employee's salary account. Settlement of the advance must be done within 10 working days of return by submitting actuals in HRMS. Any unutilised advance must be refunded to the company within the same period. Outstanding unsettled advances will result in the withholding of future advances.

Travel and Expense Policy > 3. Travel Approval

All business travel must be pre-approved before any bookings are made. Domestic travel requires approval from the reporting manager. International travel requires approval from the department head and HR Director. Travel approval requests must be submitted through the HRMS Travel module at least 5 working days before the travel date for domestic trips and at least 15 working days for international trips. Emergency travel approved verbally must be regularised in HRMS within 24 hours of booking.

answers.question: When is the employee referral bonus paid?
answers.ground_truth: It is paid 50 percent after the hire completes 3 months and 50 percent after 6 months, and the referrer must still be employed when each part is due.
answers.answer:
The referral bonus is paid in two equal tranches:
- The first tranche of 50 percent is paid in the payroll cycle following the completion of 3 months of continuous employment by the referred candidate from their date of joining.
- The second tranche of 50 percent is paid in the payroll cycle following the completion of 6 months of continuous employment by the referred candidate.

Eligibility and exceptions:
- The referring employee must still be employed when each tranche is due.
- Band 8+ confidential roles are excluded.
- If the referred candidate leaves voluntarily or is terminated before completing 3 months, no bonus is paid.
- If the candidate leaves or is terminated after completing 3 months but before completing 6 months, only the first tranche is paid and the second tranche is forfeited.
contexts:
Employee Referral Policy > 6. Referral Bonus Payment Timeline

The referral bonus is paid in two equal tranches to balance incentive with retention. The first tranche of 50 percent of the bonus is paid in the payroll cycle following the completion of 3 months of continuous employment by the referred candidate from their date of joining. The second tranche of 50 percent of the bonus is paid in the payroll cycle following the completion of 6 months of continuous employment by the referred candidate. If the referred candidate leaves Rutuja Talent Nexus voluntarily or is terminated before completing 3 months, no bonus is paid to the referring employee. If the referred candidate leaves or is terminated after completing 3 months but before completing 6 months, only the first tranche is paid and the second tranche is forfeited.

Employee Referral Policy > At a Glance

Submit referrals through the HRMS Referral Module before the candidate applies. The bonus is paid 50 percent after the hire completes 3 months and 50 percent after 6 months; the referrer must still be employed when each tranche is due. Band 8+ confidential roles are excluded.

Employee Referral Policy > 4. Referral Bonus Structure

The referral bonus is a one-time payment made to the referring employee upon the referred candidate successfully completing the retention period defined in Section 6. The bonus amounts are as follows by the band of the role being filled. For roles at Band 1 to Band 2, the referral bonus is Rs. 15,000. For roles at Band 3 to Band 4, the referral bonus is Rs. 30,000. For roles at Band 5 to Band 6, the referral bonus is Rs. 50,000. For roles at Band 7 and above, the referral bonus is Rs. 75,000. For niche or hard-to-fill roles designated as Priority Referral roles by the Talent Acquisition team, the referral bonus is enhanced by 50 percent over the standard rate. Priority Referral roles are listed separately on the internal job board and are updated quarterly. All referral bonuses are subject to applicable income tax deductions as per the Income Tax Act and are included in the referring employee's Form 16.

Compensation and Benefits Policy > 13. Referral Bonus

Employees who refer candidates for open positions at Rutuja Talent Nexus are eligible for a referral bonus. The referral bonus is paid in two tranches: 50 percent upon the referred employee completing 3 months of service and 50 percent upon completion of 6 months. Referral bonus amounts by grade are: Rs. 20,000 for non-technical roles, Rs. 30,000 for technical individual contributor roles, Rs. 50,000 for senior and lead roles, and Rs. 75,000 for managerial and specialist roles. Referrals must be submitted through the HRMS Referral module before the candidate applies.

Employee FAQ > 6. Joining, Probation, and Exit

How long is probation? 6 months as standard, or 3 months for Bands 1-3, extendable once by up to 3 months. Confirmation requires a clean background verification.

What is my notice period? 2 weeks while on probation and 3 months once confirmed. Notice period buyout is possible with management and HR approval.

When do I get my final settlement and relieving letter? Full and Final settlement is processed within 45 days of your last working day, and the relieving and experience letters are issued within 7 working days after FnF.

Can I refer a friend for a job? Yes. Submit the referral through the HRMS Referral Module before the candidate applies. The referral bonus is paid 50 percent when the hire completes 3 months and 50 percent at 6 months.

answers.question: How much emergency salary advance can I get?
answers.ground_truth: An emergency advance of up to Rs. 25,000 is available regardless of band.
answers.answer: You can get an emergency advance of up to Rs. 25,000 irrespective of your band, provided you have an urgent and unforeseen financial need and have not had an emergency advance in the previous 12 months.
contexts:
Salary Advance Policy > 7. Emergency Advance

In cases of urgent and unforeseen financial need, an employee may apply for an emergency advance of up to Rs. 25,000 irrespective of their band, provided they have not had an emergency advance in the previous 12 months. The emergency advance is processed within 2 working days of approval. It is recovered in a single deduction in the following month's payroll. Employees who receive an emergency advance remain ineligible for a regular salary advance until the emergency advance is fully repaid and a further 3 months have elapsed.

Salary Advance Policy > 5. Advance Limits

The maximum salary advance an eligible employee may receive in a single application is as follows based on their band. Employees at Band 1 to Band 3 are eligible for an advance of up to 1 month's gross salary. Employees at Band 4 to Band 5 are eligible for an advance of up to 1.5 months' gross salary. Employees at Band 6 and above are eligible for an advance of up to 2 months' gross salary. In all cases, the advance amount shall not exceed Rs. 2,50,000. Requests for amounts higher than these limits require explicit approval from the HR Director and the Chief Financial Officer and will be considered only in exceptional documented circumstances such as major medical emergencies or natural disasters.

Salary Advance Policy > At a Glance

Confirmed employees with 12+ months of service can take an interest-free salary advance (up to 1 month's gross salary for Bands 1-3; higher limits for senior bands), repaid through equal payroll deductions. An emergency advance of up to Rs. 25,000 is available regardless of band. Outstanding balances are recovered from the Full and Final settlement.

Salary Advance Policy > 3. Definition of Salary Advance

A salary advance is a portion of an employee's future salary disbursed early by the company, to be recovered through subsequent payroll deductions over an agreed repayment period. It is not a loan, does not carry any interest, and is recovered entirely from the employee's own future salary. A salary advance is distinct from an emergency advance, which is a smaller, faster disbursement described in Section 7 of this policy.

Salary Advance Policy > 1. Policy Brief and Purpose

This policy governs the process by which eligible employees of Rutuja Talent Nexus Pvt. Ltd. may request an advance on their salary in cases of genuine personal financial need. Rutuja Talent Nexus recognises that employees may occasionally face unexpected financial hardship and aims to provide a fair, structured, and interest-free mechanism to support them without burdening them with exploitative terms. This policy establishes eligibility criteria, advance limits, repayment terms, and the process for requesting and approving salary advances.

answers.question: How soon must I file a sexual harassment complaint?
answers.ground_truth: Complaints must be filed with the Internal Complaints Committee within 3 months of the incident.
answers.answer: You must file a written complaint with the ICC within 3 months of the date of the incident or the last incident in a series of incidents.
contexts:
Prevention of Sexual Harassment Policy (POSH) > 5. Filing a Complaint

An aggrieved employee who experiences or witnesses sexual harassment may file a written complaint with the ICC at their respective office location. The complaint must be submitted within 3 months of the date of the incident or the last incident in a series of incidents. The complaint should include the name and employee ID of the complainant, the name of the respondent, the date, time, and place of the incident, a detailed description of the incident, names of any witnesses, and any supporting evidence such as screenshots, emails, or messages. In cases where the complainant is unable to file a written complaint due to physical or mental incapacity, a complaint may be filed on their behalf by a legal heir, friend, or colleague with the ICC's permission. The ICC will provide a written acknowledgment of the complaint within 7 working days.

Prevention of Sexual Harassment Policy (POSH) > 6. Inquiry Process

Upon receipt of the complaint, the ICC will conduct a time-bound inquiry as follows. The ICC will send a copy of the complaint to the respondent within 7 working days of receipt, requesting a written response within 10 working days. Both parties will be given equal opportunity to present their case and evidence. The inquiry will be conducted with strict confidentiality. The ICC may interview witnesses and examine documentary evidence. The ICC will complete its inquiry and submit a report to the employer within 60 days of receiving the complaint. The report will contain a finding of facts and a recommendation on action to be taken. The employer will act on the ICC recommendation within 60 days of receiving the report.

Prevention of Sexual Harassment Policy (POSH) > At a Glance

Zero tolerance for sexual harassment under the POSH Act 2013. File complaints with the Internal Complaints Committee (Presiding Officer: Ms. Priya Deshmukh) within 3 months of the incident; a time-bound inquiry follows with interim relief available. Reach the ICC at icc@rutujatalentnexus.in.

Prevention of Sexual Harassment Policy (POSH) > 7. Interim Relief

During the pendency of the inquiry, the ICC may recommend interim relief measures to protect the complainant. These may include transferring the complainant or the respondent to a different team or location, granting special leave to the complainant, or restraining the respondent from reporting on or evaluating the complainant's work.

Prevention of Sexual Harassment Policy (POSH) > 9. False Complaints

If the ICC finds that the complaint was false or malicious and made with the intent to harm the respondent, appropriate action may be taken against the complainant. However, the inability to substantiate a complaint will not be treated as a false complaint.

answers.question: What should I do if my company laptop is stolen?
answers.ground_truth: Loss or theft requires an FIR filed within 48 hours.
answers.answer: If your company laptop is stolen, you must file a First Information Report (FIR) with the local police immediately and submit a copy to HR and IT within 48 hours of the incident.
contexts:
IT Asset and Equipment Policy > 7. Loss, Theft, and Damage > 7.2. Loss or Theft

In the event of loss or theft of company equipment, the employee must file a First Information Report (FIR) with the local police immediately and submit a copy to HR and IT within 48 hours of the incident. All lost or stolen devices will be remotely wiped by the IT team to prevent data breaches. The employee will bear 50 percent of the depreciated replacement cost of the lost or stolen device if it is determined that the loss occurred due to negligence such as leaving the device unattended in a public space. The depreciated value is calculated based on the company's standard asset depreciation schedule.

IT Asset and Equipment Policy > At a Glance

Every employee is issued a company laptop with full-disk encryption, endpoint protection, and VPN. Report damage within 24 hours; loss or theft needs an FIR filed within 48 hours. All assets must be returned by the last working day. A physical asset audit runs every January.

Employee FAQ > 7. IT, Security, and Conduct

My laptop is lost or stolen. What do I do? File an FIR with the local police immediately and share a copy with IT and HR within 48 hours. IT will remotely wipe the device. For damage, report to the IT helpdesk within 24 hours.

Can I use ChatGPT or other AI tools for work? Only tools on the company's Approved AI Tools List, and never with confidential, client, or personal data. Review everything an AI tool produces before using it. See the AI Tool Usage Policy.

Can I do freelance work on the side? Not without prior written approval. Moonlighting and competing engagements are prohibited; unpaid volunteering and academic guest lectures with a small honorarium are exempt. See the Moonlighting and Conflict of Interest Policy.

How do I report harassment or an ethics concern? For sexual harassment, write to the Internal Complaints Committee at icc@rutujatalentnexus.in within 3 months of the incident. For fraud or ethics concerns, use ethics@rutujatalentnexus.in (anonymous reports accepted). For other grievances, use the HRMS Grievance Module or grievance@rutujatalentnexus.in.

IT Asset and Equipment Policy > 6. Employee Responsibilities for Asset Care

The employee is responsible for keeping assigned equipment in good working condition. The employee must use the provided laptop bag or protective sleeve when transporting the device. The employee must not expose the equipment to extreme temperatures, liquids, or physical impact. The employee must report any malfunction, damage, or loss to the IT helpdesk at it-helpdesk@rutujatalentnexus.in within 24 hours of the incident. The employee must ensure that all company data is backed up to the approved cloud storage or version control systems and must not rely solely on local storage. The employee must keep the device locked with an approved password and must not share login credentials with anyone.

IT Asset and Equipment Policy > 7. Loss, Theft, and Damage > 7.1. Accidental Damage

In the event of accidental damage to company equipment, the employee must report the incident to the IT helpdesk and HR within 24 hours. IT will assess the damage and determine whether it is covered under the company's equipment insurance policy. First-time incidents of accidental damage caused by genuine carelessness will not attract a financial penalty. However, a formal warning may be issued if the damage is found to result from gross negligence. Repeated instances of accidental damage within the same financial year will attract a partial cost recovery from the employee.

answers.question: What happens to my vested ESOP options if I resign?
answers.ground_truth: On resignation, vested options must be exercised within 90 days.
answers.answer: In case of voluntary resignation, vested but unexercised options must be exercised within 90 days of the last working day, failing which they will lapse.
contexts:
Employee Stock Ownership Plan (ESOP) Policy > 9. Treatment of Options on Separation

In case of voluntary resignation, unvested options will lapse on the last working day. Vested but unexercised options must be exercised within 90 days of the last working day, failing which they will lapse. In case of termination for cause, all options whether vested or unvested will be forfeited with immediate effect on the termination date. In case of retirement, all unvested options will vest on a pro-rated basis as of the retirement date and may be exercised within 180 days. In case of death or permanent disability, all unvested options will vest immediately and the employee or their legal nominee may exercise them within 180 days of the event.

Employee Stock Ownership Plan (ESOP) Policy > At a Glance

8 percent of fully diluted equity (about 680,000 shares) is reserved for the ESOP pool. Options are granted each April at a Fair Market Value exercise price and vest over 4 years on a cliff-and-graded schedule. On resignation, vested options must be exercised within 90 days. Manage grants at esop.rutujatalentnexus.in.

Employee Stock Ownership Plan (ESOP) Policy > 8. Liquidity Events

In the event of a Liquidity Event such as an Initial Public Offering (IPO), merger, acquisition, or strategic sale of Rutuja Talent Nexus, unvested options may be accelerated at the discretion of the Board. In an IPO scenario, all unvested options will vest immediately upon listing. Upon an acquisition or merger, the acquirer may choose to honour existing grants, replace them with equivalent grants in the acquiring entity, or accelerate vesting of unvested options as part of the deal terms. Employees will be notified of specific treatment of their ESOP grants in the event of a Liquidity Event at the earliest opportunity.

Employee Stock Ownership Plan (ESOP) Policy > 12. Confidentiality

ESOP grant details including the number of options, exercise price, and vesting schedule are confidential information. Employees must not disclose their ESOP grant details to colleagues or external parties as this information is commercially sensitive.

Employee Stock Ownership Plan (ESOP) Policy > 6. Vesting Schedule

Options vest over a 4-year period from the date of grant following a cliff-and-graded schedule. The vesting schedule is as follows. No options vest in the first 12 months from the grant date. This is known as the cliff period. After 12 months from the grant date, 25 percent of granted options vest at once. Thereafter, an additional 25 percent of the remaining options vest at the end of each subsequent 12-month period. The full vesting schedule is: Year 1 (cliff) is 0 percent, Year 2 is 25 percent, Year 3 is 50 percent, Year 4 is 75 percent, and Year 5 is 100 percent of total options granted. Example: An employee granted 1000 options in April 2024 will have 0 options vested by April 2025, 250 options vested by April 2026, 500 options vested by April 2027, 750 options vested by April 2028, and 1000 options fully vested by April 2029.

answers.question: What is the sum insured under the group health insurance?
answers.ground_truth: The base sum insured is Rs. 5,00,000 per policy year.
answers.answer: The base sum insured under the group health insurance is Rs. 5,00,000 (or Rs. 5 lakh) per policy year / per employee per annum, which is a floater amount shared across the employee and all enrolled dependents within the same policy year. Additionally, employees may opt for a top-up cover of Rs. 5 lakh at an additional premium deducted from their salary.
contexts:
Group Health Insurance and Mediclaim Policy > 4. Coverage and Sum Insured > 4.1. Employee Coverage

All covered employees receive a base sum insured of Rs. 5,00,000 per policy year for hospitalisation expenses. This covers the employee as the primary insured member.

Group Health Insurance and Mediclaim Policy > At a Glance

Base sum insured is Rs. 5,00,000 per policy year; spouse and children up to age 25 are covered at no cost, and parents can be added at a 50 percent subsidised premium. Cashless treatment is available at 8,000+ network hospitals; reimbursement claims are due within 30 days of discharge. The enrolment window opens every March.

Employee FAQ > 4. Insurance and Benefits

What health insurance do I have? A group mediclaim policy with a base sum insured of Rs. 5,00,000 per policy year, covering you, your spouse, and children up to age 25 at no cost. Parents can be added at a 50 percent subsidised premium.

How do I use cashless hospitalisation? Present your insurance e-card (downloadable from the HRMS Benefits section) at any of the 8,000+ network hospitals. For planned admissions, request pre-authorisation through the insurer helpline listed on your e-card.

What other benefits do I get? Group term life insurance at 3 times annual CTC, EPF, gratuity after 5 years of service, corporate NPS with a company contribution for eligible opted-in employees, and a Flexible Benefits Plan for Band 4 and above. See the Compensation and Benefits Policy.

Group Health Insurance and Mediclaim Policy > 4. Coverage and Sum Insured > 4.2. Dependent Coverage

Each employee may enrol the following dependents under the group mediclaim policy at no additional cost to the employee. The eligible dependents are the employee's legally married spouse, and dependent children up to the age of 25 years. The sum insured of Rs. 5,00,000 is a floater amount shared across the employee and all enrolled dependents within the same policy year.

Compensation and Benefits Policy > 8. Health Insurance

Rutuja Talent Nexus provides group health insurance coverage to all employees and their dependents. The sum insured under the group mediclaim policy is Rs. 5 lakh per employee per annum. Coverage includes the employee, spouse or partner, up to 2 dependent children below 25 years of age, and dependent parents or parents-in-law subject to an additional premium paid by the employee. Pre-existing conditions are covered from day one of joining. Maternity expenses are covered up to Rs. 75,000 per delivery. Dental and vision care are not included in the group policy. Employees may opt for a top-up cover of Rs. 5 lakh at an additional premium deducted from their salary. The HR team coordinates all insurance-related queries through the designated insurance broker.
